City council approves new tram line

By Jana Novak, 12 March 2026

The city council voted on Tuesday night to approve a new tram line connecting the northern suburbs with the central station, ending a debate that has lasted almost six years.

Construction is expected to begin in the spring of 2027 and to take about three years, according to the transport department, which said that the total cost is estimated at 480 million crowns.

"This is the biggest investment in public transport in a generation," said the mayor.

What changes for commuters

Buses on the two busiest routes will be reduced as the tram opens, and the council promised that fares will stay the same for at least two years after the opening day.

  • Journey time from the north falls from 42 to 25 minutes
  • Trams every six minutes at peak times
  • Eleven new stops, all step-free

Residents along the route can raise concerns at an open meeting on 4 April, and the council said that every written objection will receive an answer.
